name: Chisel
text:
**Decision:** Enforce a *strict human-only "Speaker Attribution Map"* live doc during earnings calls, updated in real time by a dedicated Transcripts specialist. Product owns final review but only intervenes for disputes.

**Why:** Human moderation eliminates AI misattributions in rapid-fire Q&A, preventing irreversible reputational damage from false quotes. The trade-off is slower post-call cleanup, but accuracy outweighs speed here.

name: Sift
text: **Risk:** A strict human-only live doc still fails when the Transcripts specialist misses an interruption or mishears a name—disputes won’t vanish, just shift from AI errors to human ones. **Better alternative:** Keep the hybrid model but tighten the review loop: AI tags in real time, Transcripts specialist corrects within 90 seconds, and Product only intervenes if the confidence score drops below 85%. **Settle it:** Run a 3-call pilot with this rule, measure quote disputes per call, and pick the faster, lower-error method.

name: Scope
text:
**Decision:** Use a *strict human-only live doc* with a dedicated Transcripts specialist logging speaker changes in real time, no AI tagging. Product owns final review.

**Why:** Human moderation eliminates AI misattributions during chaotic Q&A, preventing irreversible quote disputes. Trade-off: slower real-time updates, but accuracy outweighs speed.

name: Scriv
text: **Risk:** A strict human-only live doc assumes a Transcripts specialist can flawlessly track speakers in real time—fatigue, accents, or rapid interruptions will still cause errors, just slower. **Better alternative:** Keep the hybrid model but shorten the review window to *real-time corrections* by the Transcripts specialist, with AI flagging only high-confidence disputes for Product. **Settle it:** Run a 2-call pilot with both models, measure quote disputes and cleanup time—data wins.

name: Reel
text:
**Decision:** Run a *strict human-only live doc* with a dedicated Transcripts specialist logging speaker changes in real time, no AI tagging. Product owns the final review but only intervenes on disputes.

Trade-off: We accept slower post-call cleanup and higher labor cost, but eliminate the risk of irreversible quote misattribution during rapid-fire Q&A.

name: Scriv
text: **Risk:** A strict human-only live doc assumes a Transcripts specialist can parse every interruption, off-script comment, and rapid-fire analyst in real time—fatigue will force them to guess, and disputes will still arise, just slower. **Better alternative:** Keep the hybrid model but tighten the AI’s confidence threshold—only auto-tag when certainty is >95%, forcing human review for the rest. **Settle it:** Run a 2-call pilot with this threshold; if disputes drop below 5%, adopt it. If not, default to human-only.
